title: Gap junctions merge cells into a larger Self by erasing signal ownership

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Gap junctions merge cells into a larger Self by erasing signal ownership

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Because signals passing through gap junctions carry no marker of their cell of origin, gap-junctional coupling partially erases informational (memory) boundaries between cells, which promotes the formation of a larger Self whose parts work toward common goals.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2022, Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds › Somatic Cognition: An Example of Unconventional Agency in Detail › A Bioelectric Model of the Scaling of the Self

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Thus, this property of GJ coupling promotes the creation of a larger Self by partially erasing the mnemic boundaries between the parts which might impair their ability to work toward a common goal.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds”, Frontiers in systems neuroscience (2022), doi:10.3389/fnsys.2022.768201; section “Somatic Cognition: An Example of Unconventional Agency in Detail › A Bioelectric Model of the Scaling of the Self”. Scope: Gap-junction-coupled cell collectives in metazoan tissues

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2022-tame-22: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.42

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Information diffusion and coordinated responses can be quantified. The transition from those observables to a larger Self is conceptual, so existing data resolve only the mechanistic proxy.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Trace labeled signals through gap-junction-coupled cells and test whether coupling reduces source-identification accuracy while increasing coordinated pursuit of a shared measurable setpoint relative to uncoupled controls.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Matched coupling perturbation datasets are sparse.

Signal source erasure does not uniquely imply a larger Self.

Shared goals and mnemic boundaries lack standard measures.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data adequacy: 0.28
operationalizability: 0.46
analysis feasibility: 0.58
discriminating power: 0.35
data existence: 0.48

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Gap junctions pass small molecules without tagging the sender, which follows from the structure of the pore and is already standard physiology. The further claim that this erasure creates a larger Self working toward common goals uses those same coupling facts. No additional observation would favor the Self wording over shared signals through open junctions.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Tracer studies can show that material crossing a gap junction carries no origin label, and the same records are what a larger Self and ordinary shared cytoplasm both predict.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value: Loss of a diffusion barrier and formation of a larger Self predict the same coupling, coordination, and shared signals.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:

analysis feasibility: 0.15
operationalizability: 0.2
data adequacy: 0.1
data existence: 0.15
